events.credibility_reason: One-line abstract claiming all four Landau problems with no argument on the page; 27 years with no uptake; every later source still lists the problems open.

Elementary Wilson's-theorem argument whose contradiction step appears circular (an irrationality lemma applied to a rational ratio); six rapid revisions changing definitions; no uptake in six years; later sources still call the problem open and do not cite it. The circularity is the researcher's own check, so not treated as knocked_down.
Infinitude claimed as one item in an abstract of an 'elementary' geometric theory in math.GM; venue refereeing unverified; no uptake; later sources still call it open.
Statement appears reformulated with an integer shift c and changes across versions; no expert response.

Claims all of Bunyakovsky (degree ≥2 open, a landmark) with no argument and an undefined 'AION' framework; same author posts AION 'resolutions' of Goldbach, BSD, Beal and Riemann on an unreviewed platform; no uptake; Wikipedia (June 2026) and AIM list (May 2026) still call the problem open.
Exponent 1.317 conflicts with the 1.312 stated in the source it cites, unexplained.

Claims the full Bateman–Horn conjecture (a landmark) via Golomb's method, which is known to rest on an unjustified limit–series interchange; serial companion claims (Schinzel, Chowla) within months; no expert uptake or journal; Wikipedia (June 2026) and AIM (May 2026) still list the problem as open.

events.ai_basis: Corollary 1.2 and its initial proof were first obtained in an autonomous way by the AI model ChatGPT-5.6 Sol Pro after a single prompt in July 2026.

why: The statement asks only whether n²+1 is prime infinitely often. Lower bounds on the largest prime factor P(n²+1), almost-prime results, primitive-divisor counts, square divisors of shifted primes and p²+nq² primes are different questions sharing the polynomial, not bounds on any quantity the statement asks for; none can produce a prime value. I scored them variant rather than bound, which was the close call for Pasten 2026 and Pascadi: their titles invoke n²+1 but the quantity is not the problem's. Pasten 2026's own acknowledgement credits the AI with autonomously obtaining Corollary 1.2 and its initial proof, so its ai_role is generated for that event, but the event is a variant. Grantham–Graves is a finite census (instances). The claimed full proofs (Liu, Vega, Acevedo, Aabidi El Moussati, Xiao) each combine no uptake on a landmark problem, later sources still calling it open, and either no argument, a known-gap method, or serial claims on other famous conjectures, so they are not_credible. Sopin proves a shifted reformulation (variant).
doubts: Xiao's full text was never reached (HTTP 403) and its AI involvement unchecked; the not_credible call rests on the abstract snippet and the known gap in Golomb's method. Vega's circularity is the researcher's own reading of excerpts. A reader who counts largest-prime-factor lower bounds as progress on Landau's fourth problem would score Pascadi, Grimmelt–Merikoski and Pasten 2026 as bound instead of variant; I did not, because the statement names no such quantity. Pasten 2026's AI quote came from summarising fetches of the HTML, not a verbatim read.
